title: Tiger Reserves, Project Tiger and the Tiger Census

cards.b:
The tiger is a favourite of both Prelims and Mains. Questions ask for the launch year of Project Tiger, the NTCA's status, census numbers, and zones inside a reserve.

It is also the best example of an umbrella species policy.

Watch the dates: the Act is 1972, the project is 1973, and the statutory NTCA is 2006.

Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 with nine reserves, starting with Jim Corbett. It followed a fall in tiger numbers to about 1,800 in the early 1970s. It is a centrally sponsored scheme, now under the MoEFCC.

The Wildlife (Protection) Act was amended in 2006 to create the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) as a statutory body. The same amendment set up the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (2007) to fight poaching and trade.

Under Section 38V of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, a tiger reserve has:

  • Core or critical tiger habitat: legally inviolate, no human activity, declared by the state with expert advice.
  • Buffer or peripheral area: a mixed-use area for co-existence.

Village relocation from the core must be voluntary and with a package, as the Forest Rights Act 2006 requires. Critical tiger habitats are to be notified after consulting local gram sabhas.

The All India Tiger Estimation is done every four years, run by the NTCA with the Wildlife Institute of India. It uses camera traps and capture-recapture statistics, not just pugmark counts.

  • 2006: 1,411
  • 2010: 1,706
  • 2014: 2,226
  • 2018: 2,967
  • 2022: 3,682 (camera-trap estimate, announced in April 2023)

India holds about 75 percent of the world's wild tigers. Madhya Pradesh has the largest number.

• Jim Corbett (Uttarakhand): oldest, 1936 as Hailey National Park.
  • Sundarbans (West Bengal): the only mangrove tiger habitat.
  • Ranthambore (Rajasthan), Bandhavgarh and Kanha (Madhya Pradesh).
  • Periyar (Kerala), Bandipur (Karnataka), Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam (Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, the largest by area).
  • Pakke and Namdapha in Arunachal Pradesh.

India has well over 50 tiger reserves.

The tiger range countries signed the St. Petersburg Declaration (2010) with the goal TX2, to double wild tigers by 2022. The Global Tiger Forum is an inter-governmental body based in New Delhi. The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 at Mysuru for seven big cats, led by India. The tiger is Endangered on the IUCN Red List and Schedule I of the WPA.

Rising numbers cause conflict in the buffer zone. Reserve boundaries are full, so tigers move out of the parks. Relocating villages is slow and costly. Critics say the model is "fortress conservation".

Supporters point to the rise from about 1,400 to over 3,600 in two decades and to better prey and water protection.

Tigers need corridors. Roads, railways and canals cut them. The Kanha-Pench corridor and Terai Arc are key. The Supreme Court and the NTCA have issued guidance on eco-sensitive zones. The NTCA also runs the M-STrIPES monitoring app. Wildlife crime remains a risk with poaching for skins and bones.

• Project Tiger: 1973, Corbett first.
  • NTCA: statutory from 2006.
  • Core: critical tiger habitat; buffer around it.
  • Census: every four years; 3,682 in 2022.
  • Tiger Day: 29 July (International Tiger Day).

Global Tiger Day was set at the 2010 St. Petersburg summit. India reported its numbers at Mysuru in April 2023, when Project Tiger completed 50 years.

Prelims-style: "Project Tiger was launched in:" (1973). "Which Act provides for tiger reserves?" (WPA 1972 amended 2006).

Mains-style: "Examine the success of Project Tiger. What new challenges does it face?" Structure: launch; numbers; legal base; successes; conflicts, corridors, relocation; way forward.

Use numbers sparingly but exactly: 1,411 to 3,682 across 2006 to 2022 is a strong line in a conclusion.

quiz.w: It began on 1 April 1973 with nine reserves.
